in_text_mentions: ntly, she sought medical advice at the endocrine clinic for further evaluation. She also mentioned that her primary care physician had reduced her thyroxin doses over the past year due to abnormal laboratory test results, and lately, she had been only on 25 mcg daily. She also gave a history of upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) every six months. By physical examination, the midline neck swelling, measuring approximately 4 x 3 cm, was non-tender and was moving with tongue protrusion (Figure 1). No palpable lymph nodes were detected. She was clinically diagnosed with a thyroglossal cyst.

in_text_mentions: Neck ultrasonography performed in clinic by the patient's endocrinologist revealed a complex cystic mass in the midline directly anterior to the trachea and above the thyroid cartilage, measuring 52 × 41 × 50 mm (Fig. 1). The patient was then referred to Dr. Kuo for surgical evaluation. Subsequent ultrasonography showed a large cystic and septated TGDC, measuring 46 × 48 × 32 mm. Fine needle aspiration revealed no malignant cells, a few groups of benign columnar cells, histiocyte-like cells, cholesterol crystals, blood, and inflammatory cells, consistent with TGDC.

in_text_mentions: A 38-year-old female presented with a three-month history of progressively enlarging midline neck mass measuring approximately 3 cm x 2 cm. The mass was asymptomatic. Examination revealed a soft, mobile mass in the midline of the neck just below the hyoid bone, which moved with swallowing and had minimal movement on tongue protrusion. The patient's thyroid function tests were within normal limits. No regional lymphadenopathy was noted. Clinical pictures are shown in Figures 1-2.

in_text_mentions: ture was observed. It showed pseudostratified ciliated columnar and squamous epithelial lining associated with thyroid follicles in the surrounding stroma (Figs 1 and 2). These thyroid follicles were bland with no papillary nuclear atypia or invasion (Fig. 3). The cyst was filled with a thin eosinophilic material (Fig. 4) Lymphocytic thyroiditis of mild severity was identified in the rest of the thyroid tissue. Based on these findings, the diagnosis of macro vesicular thyroid adenoma with ITTGDC and lymphocytic thyroiditis was made. After the surgery, the patient developed temporary dysphonia.

panels.rationale: Single H&E photomicrograph from the surgically excised specimen of a 72-year-old male patient with a thyroglossal duct cyst. The caption explicitly describes cyst tissue lined in areas by stratified squamous epithelium and, in the fibrocollagenous wall, thyroid follicles of various sizes filled with colloid; the in-text histopathology report confirms TDC with no malignant cells in this cohort. Ectopic colloid-filled thyroid follicles within the cyst wall are a classic diagnostic histologic feature of thyroglossal duct cyst, so disease attribution and finding identification are both strong. The squamous epithelial lining described in the caption is not covered by the offered respiratory-epithelial vocabulary key, so it is recorded as a proposed finding rather than forcing an incorrect key. No panel labels or seams are present, so the figure is treated as one panel.

Sistrunk operation was performed by a consultant surgeon in each of the patients (Table 1). The procedure entailed excision of the cyst, and excision of the mid portion of the hyoid bone. The duration of hospital stay was one to three days and there were no recurrences at the sixth month of follow-up. The histopathology report confirmed TDC in all patients and none was malignant. Figure 5 and Figure 6 show photomicrographs of the specimen of one of the patients with TDC and no malignant cells were seen.

panels.rationale: Single-panel photomicrograph of the excised cyst from a reported case of subglottic thyroglossal duct cyst. The caption ('Histopathology suggestive of thyroglossal duct cyst') and in-text describe a cyst wall lined by respiratory epithelium with focal squamous metaplasia, ulceration with granulation tissue, and a fibrocollagenous wall with mixed inflammatory infiltrate, matching the visible ciliated respiratory-type epithelial lining over a vascularized inflamed fibrous wall. Histology is real human-patient material, not third-party, and is directly attributable to thyroglossal duct cyst; subglottic location per the disease-focused article title makes this a less common (variant) form. in_text_mentions: was excised in toto without any complications and was sent for histopathologic examination. Gross examination revealed a dye-stained collapsed and cut opened cystic specimen measuring 2x1.5x1cm. Microscopy revealed a cyst wall lined by respiratory epithelial lining with focal squamous metaplasia. Foci of ulceration showing granulation tissue were noted. The wall was fibro collagenous with few blood vessels, mild mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate and occasional glands. There were focal fibrosis and myxoid changes. The histopathologic examination was consistent with a thyroglossal cyst (Fig 3).

panels.rationale: Contrast-enhanced axial cervical CT from a case report of malignant thyroglossal duct cyst treated with the Sistrunk procedure. The scan shows a complex cystic mass in the right parasagittal anterior neck attached to the infrahyoid muscle and bulging toward the larynx, matching the vocabulary synonym 'anterior neck cystic mass' for a hyoid-associated TGDC; TGDC is explicitly in the stated differential diagnosis and the article is disease-focused on TGDC. The off-midline right parasagittal location is a recognized less-common presentation, so typicality is variant. No panel letters appear in the image or caption; the four axial slices are presented as one radiology figure, so it is a single panel A. No clinical annotations (arrows/callouts) are present, only scanner text overlays. Age and ethnicity are not stated.

panels.figure_caption: Cervical axial CT scan with contrast. Complex cystic mass in the right parasagittal anterior colli area, appears to bulge to the level of the larynx.
in_text_mentions: then showed a complex cystic mass in the front neck area located in the right parasagittal area, sized approximately 3.9 × 3.8 × 5.5 cm, attached to the right infrahyoid muscle, appearing to bulge into the larynx, with differential diagnosis of the thyroglossal duct cyst or epidermoid cyst (Figure 1). The thyroid gland appeared to be within normal limits. The scan also discovered multiple lymph node enlargement in the submental area and along the right jugular chain that measured largest in size 22 mm in the right area and 17 mm in the left. The thyroid function test was within normal limits.

A: Real patient histopathology (H&E, 2×) of the excised thyroglossal duct cyst showing a cystic structure with a disrupted, inflamed wall (arrow) and luminal eosinophilic debris (asterisk), matching the in-text description of the inflamed TGDC; the article title confirms a pediatric TGDC case, whose lateral presentation is an atypical form. No vocabulary finding_key matches this gross-wall disruption pattern, so terms are proposed. B: Real patient histopathology (H&E, 20×) of the thyroglossal duct cyst showing an intact benign squamous epithelial lining of the cyst wall (arrow), a specific histologic manifestation of TGDC per the caption and in-text description. The vocabulary only lists respiratory (ciliated) epithelial lining, not squamous lining, so the observed feature is proposed rather than mapped. Atypical designation reflects the lateral presentation emphasized in the article title. C: Real patient histopathology (H&E, 20×) of...

panels.figure_caption: Histopathologic features of a thyroglossal duct cyst (hematoxylin and eosin). (A) Low-power view (2×) demonstrates a cystic structure with a disrupted, inflamed wall (arrow) and luminal eosinophilic debris (asterisk). (B) High-power view (20×) demonstrates an intact benign squamous epithelial lining of the cyst wall (arrow). (C) High-power view (20×) demonstrates a partially denuded squamous epithelial lining (arrow) with adjacent mixed inflammatory infiltrate (asterisk). (D) Low-power view (2×) demonstrates a marked stromal reaction with dense fibrosis and mixed inflammatory infiltrate (asterisk), with adjacent benign thyroid parenchyma showing well-formed follicles containing colloid (arrow)
in_text_mentions: n, homogeneous, gelatinous material. The cyst wall was disrupted in areas, with yellow fibrous tissue and a focal region of calcification. Histopathologic analysis demonstrated a disrupted cyst wall lined by benign squamous epithelium with a surrounding mixed acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrate and marked stromal reaction. Adjacent benign thyroid parenchyma with normal follicular architecture and colloid was identified, consistent with adherent normal thyroid tissue incorporated into the specimen during surgical excision. Overall findings were consistent with an inflamed TGDC (Figure 5).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Low-power H&E of the resected specimen showing the cyst (star) together with the hyoid bone (arrow), confirming a hyoid-associated thyroglossal duct cyst in a human patient. B: Higher-power H&E showing the cyst lining and thyroid tissue in the cyst wall (arrow), diagnostic histologic features of a thyroglossal duct cyst in a human patient; the flattened squamous lining is noted as a proposed finding since the vocabulary only lists respiratory-type lining.
panels.attribution_text: Park et al. A rare case of thyroglossal duct cyst extending to the sublingual space: A case report.. Medicine 2020. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000019389. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Thyroglossal duct cyst (hematoxylin eosin stain, magnification ×12.5 and ×100) A. The specimen shows the hyoid bone (arrow) and cyst (star). B. The cyst was lined with flattened squamous epithelium (arrow head) and shows thyroid tissue at the wall (arrow).
in_text_mentions: Excision of the cyst with the body of the hyoid bone and the track to the base of the tongue was performed. The specimen was sent for histopathologic examination. The histological hematoxylin and eosin sections showed flattened epithelium cells supported by a fibrocollagenous cyst wall. In a focal area of the cyst wall, there was a small portion of thyroid tissue (Fig. 2). The final pathologic diagnosis was a thyroglossal duct cyst. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and recurrence of the disease has not been seen for the past year.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: H&E histology (x5) of the excised thyroglossal duct cyst wall showing focal ulceration and inflammation; the in-text confirms the TGDC specimen was histologically an inflamed TGDC (Figure 3a). Real human-patient histology of the target disease; inflammation/ulceration are clearly present but not in the allowed vocabulary, so they are recorded as proposed_findings. A black arrow annotation is present. b: H&E histology (x10) of the same excised thyroglossal duct cyst wall, lined by respiratory epithelium, directly matching the vocabulary finding for a ciliated respiratory epithelial cyst lining. Real human-patient histology of the target disease; the in-text attributes Figures 3a and 3b to the TGDC specimen (the separate lymphocytic thyroiditis involved the thyroid gland, not this figure).

in_text_mentions: There were two excised specimens - the thyroid gland and the TGDC. The cystic lesion of 5.5 x 3 x 0.5 cm was excised with no abnormal gross pathology. plate_findings.evidence: lining of hyperplastic respiratory epithelium

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: H&E histopathology at 400× showing hyperplastic respiratory (pseudostratified ciliated columnar) epithelial lining of the cyst, a recognized diagnostic feature of thyroglossal duct cyst. The article title and in-text confirm a lingual TGDC in an infant; the ventral tongue presentation is explicitly rare, hence atypical. [raw subtype: lingual] B: H&E histopathology at 400× showing stratified squamous epithelial lining of the cyst wall, confirmed by in-text ('Sections revealed a thin-walled cyst lined by stratified squamous epithelium... consistent with a TGDC'). Squamous lining is a recognized TGDC feature but has no dedicated vocabulary key, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. Rare lingual presentation in an infant makes this atypical. [raw subtype: lingual]
panels.attribution_text: Pargal et al. A Rare Ventral Tongue Presentation of a Lingual Thyroglossal Duct Cyst in an Infant: A Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106705. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 6.
panels.figure_caption: Thyroglossal duct cyst from the ventral surface of the tongue showing (A) lining of hyperplastic respiratory epithelium and (B) lining of stratified squamous epithelium. The cyst wall was comprised of delicate fibrocollagenous tissue with congested blood vessels and scattered mononuclear cell infiltrates. Hematoxylin and eosin, 400×.
in_text_mentions: Gross examination revealed a dark-brown cystic soft-tissue mass measuring 4 × 1.5 × 0.2 cm. The cut section showed the cyst to be thin-walled with an irregular inner lining. No papillary excrescences or nodularities were identified, grossly. Sections revealed a thin-walled cyst lined by stratified squamous epithelium, with focal areas showing hyperplastic respiratory epithelial lining. The wall consisted of delicate fibrocollagenous tissue with congested blood vessels. No thyroid tissue or neoplastic pathology was identified. The features were consistent with a TGDC (Figure 6).

A: Real patient H&E of the resected specimen; ectopic thyroid follicles in the fibrous cyst wall are the textbook diagnostic histology of a thyroglossal duct cyst and match the vocabulary finding directly. Article is disease-focused (mediastinal TGDC) and the in-text final diagnosis is benign mediastinal TGDC. [raw subtype: mediastinal] B: Real patient H&E of the same resected TGDC specimen showing the cyst epithelial lining (attenuated squamous-to-cuboidal), a recognized lining of TGDC. Not a diagram/control/other disease; the squamous-to-cuboidal lining is not the ciliated respiratory lining in the vocabulary, so it is captured as a proposed finding rather than misattributed to the respiratory-lining key. [raw subtype: mediastinal] C: Real patient H&E of the resected TGDC showing stratified keratinizing squamous epithelium lining the cyst, a recognized (less common) lining pattern for TGDC. panels.figure_caption: Histopathological examination of the resected specimen (haematoxylin and eosin stain). (A) Ectopic follicular thyroid tissue within the fibrous cyst wall. (B) Attenuated squamous-to-cuboidal epithelial lining. (C) Stratified keratinizing squamous epithelium. (D) Foreign-body giant-cell reaction and chronic inflammatory infiltrate. Original magnification ×40; scale bars = 500 micrometres.
in_text_mentions: Gross pathology showed a 16.5-g cystic specimen measuring 5 × 4 × 3.2 cm. Histology demonstrated a cyst lined predominantly by stratified squamous epithelium and focally by attenuated cuboidal/ columnar epithelium, with mature thyroid follicles in the fibrous cyst wall and a foreign-body giant-cell reaction (Fig. 4). There was no epithelial dysplasia or malignancy. The final diagnosis was a benign mediastinal TGDC.

The group with a history of RIT showed a higher prevalence of TGDCs than those without, but no statistical difference was found (p = 0.062). plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'solid soft tissue mass containing high signal hyperintensity, cystic changes, and invasion of the infrahyoid muscles' — anterior neck cystic/solid mass of the thyroglossal duct cyst

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial contrast MRI of a real human patient from a case report focused on papillary carcinoma arising de novo in a thyroglossal duct cyst. The caption and in-text directly attribute this anterior neck mass (with cystic changes and infrahyoid muscle invasion) to the thyroglossal duct cyst workup that led to Sistrunk procedure, so the panel visibly shows a specific manifestation of the configured disease. The complex solid-cystic invading mass represents the uncommon malignant-transformation presentation rather than a simple classic cyst, hence variant typicality. [raw subtype: papillary carcinoma (malignant transformation of TDC)] B: Coronal MRI of the same real patient showing the craniocaudal extent of the anterior neck thyroglossal duct cyst mass with cystic changes and infrahyoid muscle invasion. The caption, in-text, and disease-focused article title (papillary carcinoma of thyroglossal duct cyst) support attribution to the configured...

plate_findings.evidence: Purely cystic thyroglossal lesion.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel A is a real patient ultrasound showing a purely cystic thyroglossal duct lesion, classic TGC-TIRADS 2 appearance. B: Panel B is a real patient ultrasound of a thyroglossal duct cyst with internal echoes, corresponding to TGC-TIRADS 3. C: Panel C is a real patient ultrasound showing a well-defined solid cystic thyroglossal lesion without vascularity or calcification, TGC-TIRADS 4A. D: Panel D is a real patient ultrasound of a thyroglossal duct lesion with internal calcifications, TGC-TIRADS 4B. E: Panel E is a real patient ultrasound showing a thyroglossal solid cystic lesion with irregular margins and calcifications, TGC-TIRADS 4C. F: Panel F is a real patient ultrasound of a thyroglossal solid cystic lesion with irregular margins, calcifications and vascularity, TGC-TIRADS 5.

(D) TGC-TIRADS 4B: Well defined solid cystic lesion with internal calcifications. (E) TGC-TIRADS 4C: Solid cystic lesion with irregular margins and internal calcifications. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial contrast-enhanced neck CT of an adult patient showing a large, homogeneous, non-enhancing midline cystic lesion in the infrahyoid region, the hallmark CT appearance of a thyroglossal duct cyst; article title ('Giant thyroglossal duct cyst in an adult: CT findings'), caption, and in-text diagnosis of TGDC confirm attribution. B: Sagittal contrast-enhanced neck CT reconstruction demonstrating the midline cystic lesion's inferior relationship to the hyoid bone, consistent with the diagnosed thyroglossal duct cyst per the article title, caption, and in-text statement that a diagnosis of TGDC was established.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial preoperative neck CT of the reported case; the arrow marks a large circumscribed cystic lesion in the anterior neck. The caption and in-text explicitly identify it as a thyroglossal duct cyst extending from the hyoid bone toward the thyroid isthmus, a real patient radiology image of the target disease. B: Sagittal preoperative neck CT of the reported case; the arrow marks the cyst extending through the anterior neck space just below the hyoid bone. The caption and in-text attribute this cystic lesion to a thyroglossal duct cyst, making it a real patient image showing a specific manifestation of the target disease.

panels.figure_caption: preoperative neck computed tomography of the reported case: A) axial scan; the arrow indicates the thyroglossal duct cyst measuring 8.7 cm axially and 6.6 cm anteroposteriorly; B) sagittal scan; the arrow indicates the cyst extending throughout the anterior neck space just below the hyoid bone
in_text_mentions: Diagnostic assessment: the rest of the clinical examination, upper airway endoscopy, and labs were beyond normal range. A computed tomography (CT) scan was conducted, and it revealed a circumscribed cystic lesion extending from the hyoid bone to the thyroid isthmus, measuring 8.7 cm axially, 6.6 cm anteroposteriorly, and 6.4 cm craniocaudally, that did not exhibit contrast enhancement (Figure 2A, Figure 2B). A clinical diagnosis of a TGDC was made based on history, clinical and radiographic findings.

panels.rationale: Single sagittal contrast CT of the neck (panel A) from a disease-focused article on papillary thyroid carcinoma arising in a thyroglossal duct cyst. The caption and in-text directly describe a cystic tubular structure (red arrow) in the anterior midline neck, which is the CT manifestation of a thyroglossal duct cyst/tract, establishing attribution to the configured disease thyroglossal_duct_cyst rather than to the carcinoma complication alone. The red arrowhead marks a solid peripherally hyperattenuating, centrally hypoattenuating lesion with punctate calcifications (the intracyctic carcinoma component); these are clearly present but absent from the allowed vocabulary, so they are listed as proposed findings. The CT appearance of a cystic tubular thyroglossal tract is the classic presentation. Age group 'adult' is taken from the article title's explicit 'Young Adult' statement. No skin-tone or ethnicity assessment is applicable/available; red arrow and arrowhead annotations are present.

in_text_mentions: Follow-up computed tomography (CT) of the neck with contrast, in sagittal reformat and axial view, demonstrated a cystic and tubular structure slightly to the right of midline, corresponding to the abnormality visualized on ultrasound (Figures 3, 4). There was a peripherally hyperattenuating and centrally hypoattenuating lesion in the superior midline aspect of the cyst with multiple adjacent punctate calcifications measuring 1.0 x 1.2 x 1.3 cm; this finding corresponded to the area of increased echogenicity on ultrasound.

panels.rationale: Single H&E photomicrograph of the excised cyst from a human case of infected thyroglossal duct cyst. Caption and in-text explicitly state the section shows columnar and flattened epithelial lining with focal aggregates of chronic inflammatory cells in a fibrocollagenous wall, confirming the diagnosis of infected thyroglossal cyst. The columnar epithelial lining maps to the respiratory epithelial cyst lining finding; the chronic inflammatory infiltrate is not in the vocabulary and is proposed. Arrow annotation present. No age, ethnicity, or skin assessment applicable to a histology slide. [raw subtype: infected]
panels.attribution_text: Gandhi et al. Infected thyroglossal duct cyst involving submandibular region: a case report.. Case reports in dentistry 2011. doi:10.1155/2011/978263. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Photomicrograph (haematoxylin and eosin section; ×10 magnification) showing columnar and flattened epithelium of cyst with focal aggregate of chronic inflammatory cells supported by fibrocollagenous cyst wall.
in_text_mentions: and blood chemistry revealed no abnormality. After assessment, provisional diagnosis of infected thyroglossal cyst was given. The cyst was surgically excised completely, under general anesthesia, and postoperative healing was uneventful. The specimen was sent to histopathologic examination. The histological haematoxylin and eosin section showed columnar and flattened epithelium lining of cyst with focal aggregates of chronic inflammatory cells supported by fibrocollagenous cyst wall (Figure 3). These histopathological findings confirmed the provisional diagnosis of infected thyroglossal cyst.

in_text_mentions: gment attached to it. The histopathological report revealed a cystic lesion and a tumor characterized by the proliferation of columnar cells in a single layer, mostly arranged in papillae, but also in follicles, supported by a richly vascularized connective tissue. The cells had ovoid, ground glass nuclei (“Orphan Annie” eye), sometimes with grooves and pseudoinclusions (Figures 2(a)–2(h)). The tumor measured 1.4 centimeter. There was minimal infiltration of the adjacent fibroadipose tissue. This histology was compatible with papillary carcinoma in the TDC and it was staged as pT3c N0 M0 [16].

in_text_mentions: with a cervical CT-angiogram, revealing a midline cystic multiseptated lobular lesion of 31x17x31 mm that correlated with the thyroglossal duct, and with a solid component anterior to the hyoid bone. This intracystic solid component measured 10x7x14 mm, was spontaneously dense, and had contrast enhancement, probably corresponding to ectopic thyroid tissue with focal papillary carcinoma (Figure 3). This mass was adherent but did not invade the hyoid bone which showed cortical integrity, and had an intramuscular component in the base of the tongue. There were no suspicious cervical lymph nodes.

panels.rationale: Single-panel grayscale ultrasound from a case report of thyroglossal duct cyst. The image shows an anechoic, well-circumscribed cystic mass superior to the thyroid gland, matching the in-text description of a capsulated anechoic mass above the thyroid shown in Figure 2. The caption's focus on a homogeneous thyroid gland does not negate the visible cystic lesion, which is the classic sonographic appearance of a thyroglossal duct cyst. Real patient image, no third-party copyright.
panels.attribution_text: Taha et al. Thyroglossal Duct Cyst, a Case Report and Literature Review.. Diseases (Basel, Switzerland) 2022. doi:10.3390/diseases10010007. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.

in_text_mentions: Laboratory results showed that the patient was euthyroid, and his anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) was negative. Ultrasound imaging showed an echogenic, homogeneous thyroid with a total volume of 7 mL, with no intra-thyroid nodules. It also showed a mass above the thyroid gland, slightly to the right of the midline. The mass was approximately 0.041 m × 0.044 m × 0.033 m with a strong connective tissue capsule and an anechoic internal structure, as shown in Figure 2.

in_text_mentions: The radiology report suggested a bilobed thyroglossal duct cyst. He was given antibiotics for a suspected cyst infection. One month after he originally presented to the clinic, he returned with resolved erythema but complained of residual discomfort in the area. Computed tomography with contrast was performed and revealed two midline neck masses (Figure 2). There was a well-defined 1.7×1.7×1.0 cm, non-rim enhancing, low attenuation mass inferior to the thyroid gland. Another well-defined 1.2×1.1×1.6 cm, non-rim enhancing, low attenuation mass inferior to the hyoid bone/superior to the isthmus.

panels.rationale: Axial contrast CT of the neck in a patient with thyroglossal duct cyst. The image shows a cystic tubular structure slightly to the right of the midline (red arrow), consistent with a thyroglossal duct cyst/tract at the level of the hyoid bone. A peripherally hyperattenuating and centrally hypoattenuating lesion with punctate calcifications (red arrowhead) is present within the cyst, corresponding to the papillary carcinoma component described in the article. The panel is a real patient image with clear disease attribution to thyroglossal duct cyst. The presentation is a variant because papillary carcinoma arising in a thyroglossal duct cyst is a recognized but uncommon form.
panels.attribution_text: Turfe et al. Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Arising in a Thyroglossal Duct Cyst: Radiologic and Pathologic Correlation in a Young Adult.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106617. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Axial CT of the neck with contrast. Axial CT revealed a cystic tubular structure slightly to the right of the midline (red arrow). There was a peripherally hyperattenuating and centrally hypoattenuating lesion (red arrowhead) in the superior midline aspect of the cyst with multiple adjacent punctate calcifications, measuring 1.0 x 1.2 x 1.3 cm.
in_text_mentions: Follow-up computed tomography (CT) of the neck with contrast, in sagittal reformat and axial view, demonstrated a cystic and tubular structure slightly to the right of midline, corresponding to the abnormality visualized on ultrasound (Figures 3, 4). There was a peripherally hyperattenuating and centrally hypoattenuating lesion in the superior midline aspect of the cyst with multiple adjacent punctate calcifications measuring 1.0 x 1.2 x 1.3 cm; this finding corresponded to the area of increased echogenicity on ultrasound.

plate_findings.evidence: multicystic lesion extending between the bellies of the mylohyoid muscles into the floor of the mouth and abutting the body of the hyoid

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal T2W MRI of a real patient showing a hyperintense multicystic lesion in the submental region extending between the mylohyoid bellies into the floor of mouth and abutting the hyoid, with a large cyst abutting the left submandibular gland — a recognized imaging manifestation of thyroglossal duct cyst in a disease-focused article. B: Axial post-contrast T1W MRI of the same patient showing an enhancing midline cystic component adjacent to a left paramedian cyst, corresponding to the large cystic component in the left submandibular region described in the text — part of the multicystic thyroglossal duct cyst complex.
panels.attribution_text: Smiti and Mahmood. Papillary carcinoma arising from a thyroglossal duct cyst.. The Indian journal of radiology & imaging 2009. doi:10.4103/0971-3026.50828. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2(A, B).
panels.figure_caption: Coronal T2W (A) image shows a hyperintense multicystic lesion (small arrow) extending into the floor of the mouth between the bellies of the mylohyoid (large arrow). The large cyst abuts the left submandibular gland (arrowhead). Axial post-contrast T1W image (B) shows an enhancing, midline, cystic component (arrowhead) adjacent to the left paramedian cyst (arrow)
in_text_mentions: multicystic lesion (hypointense on T1W and hyperintense on T2W images) in the submental region, extending between the bellies of the mylohyoid muscles into the floor of the mouth and abutting the body of the hyoid. A few small hypointense foci were seen on T2W images that were suggestive of calcification [Figure 2a]. A large cystic component was seen in the left submandibular region, separate from the submandibular gland and in close relationship to the strap muscles [Figure 2b]. The smaller cysts in the submental region showed peripheral enhancement on CT and foci of calcification [Figure 3].

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: 'MRI image of the neck's soft tissues (native and IV KM) showing suprahyoid thyroglossal cyst located posterior to the platysma'; axial image shows a well-defined hyperintense midline anterior neck cystic mass with annotation arrows labeling 'Thyroglossal duct cyst (TGDC)' and 'Platysma'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial native MRI explicitly captioned as showing a suprahyoid thyroglossal duct cyst posterior to the platysma; the image visibly demonstrates a hyperintense midline anterior neck cystic mass with annotation arrows identifying the TGDC and platysma. Disease attribution is directly supported by the caption and the article title (Thyroglossal Duct Cyst case report). Suprahyoid location is a recognized less common presentation, hence variant typicality. [raw subtype: suprahyoid] B: Sagittal native MRI from the same captioned series showing the suprahyoid cystic mass in the anterior neck soft tissues; the caption explicitly attributes these images to a thyroglossal duct cyst, and the article is a TDC case report. No explicit letter label exists in the image, so panels are lettered by reading order. [raw subtype: suprahyoid] C: Axial post-contrast (IV KM) MRI showing the same suprahyoid thyroglossal cyst with electronic measurement...
panels.attribution_text: Taha et al. Thyroglossal Duct Cyst, a Case Report and Literature Review.. Diseases (Basel, Switzerland) 2022. doi:10.3390/diseases10010007. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: MRI image of the neck’s soft tissues (native and IV KM) showing suprahyoid thyroglossal cyst located posterior to the platysma.
in_text_mentions: yperintense in T2 with isointense parts and was also isointense in T1 with an extension of approximately 0.041 m × 0.044 m × 0.033 m. There was minimal displacement of the hypopharynx and epiglottis with no evident connection to the thyroid gland or the tongue’s base. There was also discreet contrast-medium uptake of the wall and protein-rich fluid, indicating possible previous inflammation. We found no cervical lymphadenopathy, and the submandibular gland and parotid gland were inconspicuous. In the cervical spine, as shown in Figure 3, no significant degenerative changes could be identified.

panels.rationale: Single axial non-contrast CT slice of the neck at the hyoid level in a patient from an article on papillary carcinoma arising from a thyroglossal duct cyst. The image is real patient CT (not a diagram/control/animal) and visibly shows a hyoid-level anterior-neck/submental multicystic lesion with a calcified focus indicated by the arrow, consistent with a hyoid-associated thyroglossal duct cyst on CT. The CT finding is mapped to the hyoid-CT vocabulary item because the cyst abuts the hyoid body; the clearly present multicystic morphology and calcification are not in the vocabulary and are listed as proposed findings. Calcified/multicystic appearance is a recognized less-common form (variant), and no skin, ethnicity, age, or staging information is provided. The white arrow is an annotation.

in_text_mentions: multicystic lesion (hypointense on T1W and hyperintense on T2W images) in the submental region, extending between the bellies of the mylohyoid muscles into the floor of the mouth and abutting the body of the hyoid. A few small hypointense foci were seen on T2W images that were suggestive of calcification [Figure 2a]. A large cystic component was seen in the left submandibular region, separate from the submandibular gland and in close relationship to the strap muscles [Figure 2b]. The smaller cysts in the submental region showed peripheral enhancement on CT and foci of calcification [Figure 3].

panels.rationale: Single transverse contrast CT of the neck from a real patient in an article titled 'Locally Advanced Thyroglossal Duct Cyst Carcinoma Presenting as a Neck Mass.' The in-text localizes the mass to the level of the left side of the hyoid bone (1.8 × 2.9 cm), the classic location for a thyroglossal duct cyst, and the caption reports the measured neck mass (28.6 × 18.2 mm). The mass is hyoid-associated, supporting attribution to thyroglossal_duct_cyst in its carcinoma form (article title plus FNA showing papillary thyroid cancer). No trans-hyoid tract is described and there is no hyoid erosion, so the CT tract finding key is not used. Measurement calipers (28.6 mm, 18.2 mm) are present. Age, ethnicity, and assessable skin tone are not stated. [raw subtype: carcinoma]
panels.attribution_text: Tachamo et al. Locally Advanced Thyroglossal Duct Cyst Carcinoma Presenting as a Neck Mass.. Case reports in endocrinology 2017. doi:10.1155/2017/7014313. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.

in_text_mentions: us nodule measuring 1.5 × 0.7 × 0.7 cm, along with submandibular lymph nodes, measuring 1.7 × 0.9 × 1.3 cm on the right and measuring 2.1 × 0.9 × 1.1 cm on the left. Computed tomography (CT) of the neck revealed a lobulated soft tissue mass at the level of the left side of the hyoid bone measuring 1.8 × 2.9 cm with no evidence of erosion of the hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage (Figures 1 and 2). Fine needle aspiration biopsy of the neck mass revealed papillary thyroid cancer. The patient underwent excision of the mass and thyroglossal duct cyst via a Sistrunk procedure with total thyroidectomy.

in_text_mentions: A 76-year-old male patient with no known co-morbidities presented with a swelling in front of the neck. The swelling was present for three months. It was gradually progressing in size and was associated with occasional pain. There were no significant pressure effects associated with the swelling. There were no symptoms suggestive of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism. On examination, there was a 6 x 5 cm swelling in front of the neck anterior to the thyroid cartilage, which was moving with deglutition and protrusion of the tongue (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Neck ultrasound shows a multiseptated cystic mass in a 14-year-old female; the article is focused on thyroglossal duct cyst with papillary carcinoma, and the in-text description of a neck cyst moving with the larynx/hyoid supports thyroglossal duct cyst. The multiseptated appearance is a less common sonographic form, so classified as variant.

in_text_mentions: wallowing, the mass moved up and forward together with the larynx and hyoid bone. An ultrasound examination of the neck revealed a multisepted cyst 48 mm in diameter containing several smaller cysts, all filled with fluid contents (Figure 1). It was found that the left lobe of the thyroid gland was missing and that the right lobe was compensatory and slightly enlarged. In the area of the missing left lobe, a single cystic lesion measuring 4 mm in diameter with the sonographic characteristics of a simple cyst was visualized. No pathologically enlarged and altered cervical lymph nodes were seen.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Sagittal contrast CT of an elderly woman (article title: 'Stridor in an elderly woman: an unusual presentation of a giant thyroglossal cyst') showing a large midline anterior-neck cyst intimately related to the hyoid bone with airway compression; labeled 'Thyroglossal cyst' and 'Hyoid'. The hyoid relationship on CT supports the hyoid/tract CT finding; the giant size and elderly presentation with stridor make this a recognized less-common (variant) form rather than the classic small pediatric midline mass. b: Axial contrast CT of the same patient showing the large thyroglossal cyst in relation to the remodelled hyoid bone (labeled 'Thyroglossal cyst', 'Remodelled hyoid bone', 'Epiglottis', 'Spine'). The cyst-hyoid relationship on CT supports the hyoid/tract CT finding; hyoid remodelling is a clearly labeled observation not present in the vocabulary and is therefore proposed. Giant size in an elderly woman is a less-common (variant)...

in_text_mentions: cm cystic mass which was hypoechoic with homogenous echogenicity compressing the airway. The right carotid was found to be pushed laterally. Contrast enhanced computed tomography (CECT) showed a homogenous mass of size 14 × 10 cm on the left side extending from the hyoid to the manubrium sterni compressing the tracheal lumen to a longitudinal slit. The cyst was intimately related to the hyoid bone. There was distortion of the laryngeal framework with localized remodelling of hyoid bone (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)). Baseline haematological and biochemical parameters and chest radiograph were normal.

panels.rationale: Single-panel preoperative ultrasound from a case report of an intra-thyroid thyroglossal duct cyst. The caption and in-text describe a predominantly cystic lesion in the left thyroid (red arrow) that yielded thick dark brown fluid on US-FNAB, consistent with a TDC; the article title confirms the intra-thyroid TDC diagnosis. The white star marks an incidental parathyroid lesion (primary hyperparathyroidism), not the target disease. Intra-thyroid location is a recognized rare variant of TDC, so typicality is variant. [raw subtype: intra-thyroid]
panels.attribution_text: Chandraratnam et al. Intra-Thyroid Thyroglossal Duct Cyst Incidentally Identified in an Adult With Primary Hyperparathyroidism: A Rare Case Report and Literature Review.. Cureus 2021. doi:10.7759/cureus.20399. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound image of the left thyroid area during US-FNAB An ultrasound examination during US-FNAB revealed a hypoechoic cystic lesion (red arrow) in the left thyroid. The margins were smooth and well-defined. A few echogenic granules were observed in the capsule. An FNAB was then performed with two needle passes of a 21-gauge needle. A hypoechoic solid lesion (white star) corresponding to the site of the left parathyroid was also identified but not biopsied. US-FNAB - ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration biopsy
in_text_mentions: Preoperative US-FNAB of the predominantly cystic lesion in the left thyroid (Figure 1) produced a few drops of thick dark brown fluid. Following drainage, the lesion reduced in size by approximately 50%.

panels.rationale: Prenatal ultrasound of a human fetus showing an oral cyst at the tongue base that moves with tongue movements and lies completely outside the fetal mouth, consistent with the article's diagnosis of an unusual thyroglossal duct cyst located on the tongue base. Real patient imaging study demonstrating the pathognomonic tongue-movement association of a thyroglossal duct cyst; not a diagram, control, or other disease. [raw subtype: tongue_base]

panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound image showing how the tumor moves with the tongue movements and it is completely out of the fetal mouth.
in_text_mentions: Follow-up ultrasound scans performed every 2 weeks always showed appropriate fetal growth (75–90 percentile) and a normal amniotic fluid index. There were no changes in the measurements of the oral cyst and the most striking finding was that the fetus kept his mouth open during all examinations (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Axial contrast-enhanced CT of the neck in a human patient showing a multiseptated cystic lesion with an enhancing mural nodule (arrow) anterior to the thyroid cartilage in the sub-hyoid region. The caption, in-text description, and article title ('A Rare Case of Carcinoma in the Thyroglossal Duct Cyst of an Elderly Patient') directly attribute this to thyroglossal duct cyst with possible malignant change. The enhancing mural nodule is an atypical feature for a simple thyroglossal duct cyst, consistent with the rare carcinoma presentation described.
panels.attribution_text: Sudharsanan et al. A Rare Case of Carcinoma in the Thyroglossal Duct Cyst of an Elderly Patient.. Cureus 2017. doi:10.7759/cureus.1365. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced CT scan showing a multiseptated cystic lesion with enhancing mural nodule anterior to the thyroid cartilage (arrow).
in_text_mentions: The swelling was non-tender and had variegated consistency with some parts being cystic and others firm. Clinically, a diagnosis of the thyroglossal duct cyst (with a possible malignant change) was made. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the neck was taken which showed a well-defined heterogenous cystic lesion of 5 x 4.5 cm with multiple enhancing internal septations noted in the sub-hyoid region. A homogenously enhancing component of size 3 x 1.8 cm was noted within the above lesion (Figure 2).

A: Sagittal CT slice showing a well-defined thin-walled cystic lesion in the midline infrahyoid region extending into the hyoid bone, consistent with a thyroglossal duct cyst. [raw subtype: sublingual space extension] B: Sagittal CT slice at a different level showing the same cystic lesion in the infrahyoid region with extension into the hyoid bone toward the left mouth floor, consistent with thyroglossal duct cyst with atypical sublingual extension. [raw subtype: sublingual space extension] C: Coronal CT slice demonstrating the midline cystic lesion extending into the hyoid bone and toward the left mouth floor between the genioglossus and mylohyoid muscles, consistent with thyroglossal duct cyst with sublingual space extension. in_text_mentions: A CT scan showed a well-defined thin walled cystic lesion measuring 2.6×1.8×3.4 cm. The cystic lesion was located in the midline infrahyoid region extending into the hyoid bone, reaching to the left mouth floor, between the genioglossus muscle and the mylohyoid muscle (Fig. 1). Additionally, the CT scan showed that the thyroid gland was within the normal position.

plate_findings.evidence: cross-section of cervical ultrasound showing a septated midline cyst located above the thyroid cartilage, measuring 28x50x30 mm

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real-patient grayscale cervical ultrasound showing a septated midline cyst above the thyroid cartilage, the classic sonographic appearance of a thyroglossal duct cyst; disease attribution is supported by the panel-specific caption and the thyroglossal-cyst-focused article title. No diagram, control, or third-party content. B: Color Doppler cervical ultrasound of the same patient showing the thyroglossal cyst with a caption-described isoechoic, centrally vascularized solid component on its posterior wall. A vascularized solid intracystic component is a recognized less-common ultrasound finding in thyroglossal duct cysts; attribution follows the panel-specific caption within the thyroglossal-cyst-focused article. The solid component itself is captured as a proposed finding since the vocabulary has no ultrasound-specific key for it.
